findings.title: Required legacy canonical owner trajectory never reaches T6/T7
findings.description: The packet requires successful actual legacy and full owner trajectories through T6 and START/PAUSE/RESUME/CONTINUE. The canonical legacy preparation owner chain reaches COMMIT_READY, but ProtocolExecutionService.commit fails in unchanged RepositoryTransaction.prepare_authorization_basis: S37.ref_s34_id binds Nutrition while D.ref_s34_id binds Fitness, failing the single-proposal equality predicate at transactions.py:3979. The required selector records 1 failed / 1 passed and the full own suite records 1 failed / 105 passed. Neither the full-profile success nor the legacy preparation success satisfies the legacy positive execution oracle. The committed BLOCKED/FAIL result is honest, but DoD and merge prerequisites remain unsatisfied.
findings.required_action: Resolve the packet/consumer compatibility conflict through authorized task/governance scope, then execute every required oracle at a new immutable tested revision and obtain fresh SHA-bound reviews. Do not loosen validation bindings, forge certificates, or relabel the existing denial as a successful legacy T6/T7 trajectory. A frozen protocol change is not shown necessary by this review.

findings.title: Older shared fixture assertion exceeds permitted fixture corrections
findings.description: The protected-base assertion is generalized to include optional extra_fact in source_members. The packet permits the four enumerated six source-literal edits and says all other declared current fixture corrections are prospective source-enum corrections with dependent hashes only. This extra optional-fixture behavior is neither a source enum correction nor a dependent hash correction, so it exceeds the current explicit fixture boundary even though the file appears in the path allowlist. Runtime protocol semantics are unaffected, but task scope is not satisfied.
findings.required_action: Restore the protected-base shared assertion apart from allowed source corrections and keep duplicate-source verification within the task-owned source conformance module, or obtain explicit packet scope authorization. Rerun the required commands at the changed implementation revision and obtain fresh reviews.
